paper.title_en: An evaluation of Geant4-DNA early radiochemical yields
paper.abstract_en:
Purpose:
To evaluate Geant4-DNA for the simulation of radiochemical yields in liquid water up to 1µs after irradiation, for incident electrons, protons and alpha particles beams in the keV–MeV kinetic energy range.
Methods:
Simulations of radiochemical yields are presented as a function of time for electrons and as a function of the beam parameter 𝑀⁢𝑍2/𝐸 for protons and alpha particles. They use the “chem6” and “UHDR” reference examples available in Geant4 version 11.4.0 (December 2025). The impact of physics, chemistry and time step models is investigated, and quantitatively compared to experimental data.
Results:
The option 4 physics constructor shows better plausibility for the simulation of G-values versus time and G-values versus 𝑀⁢𝑍2/𝐸. The option 3 chemistry constructor shows a global better agreement with experimental data. The micro/mesoscopic “UHDR” example is able to reproduce “chem6” results for simulations up to 1µs.
Conclusion:
It remains difficult to clearly favor one physics or chemistry model over another because of the dispersion of experimental radiolysis data at short times. We recommend continuing experimental radiolysis measurements to help benchmark simulations.
